The actual trajectory contradicts the expected convergence pattern in both direction (negative vs positive delta) and magnitude (-0.243 absolute drop over the full route).
deviation_mechanism: Optimization instability in mid-to-lower index layers prevents precise quarter-wave phase accumulation. Specific thickness measurements show non-monotonic drift: layer index 6 oscillates between 138.0 nm (round 1) and 136.96 nm (round 4); layer index 7 jumps from 192.0 nm (round 3) to 189.6 nm (round 4); layer index 10 drifts from 130.0 nm to 138.68 nm; layer index 15 moves from 192.0 nm to 189.9 nm. These excursions of 2–4 nm break the required $\phi = \pi/2$ phase condition per period. In a distributed Bragg reflector or periodic filter, cumulative optical path error ($\Delta OPD = \sum n_i \Delta d_i$) shifts the constructive interference peak away from the target band, converting high-reflection bands into transmission leaks. The score collapse to 0.647 reflects this spectral misalignment rather than a hardware or solver crash.
